entities.summary:
Martha of Denmark was a queen of Sweden by marriage to King Birger, who ruled from 1319 to 1330. Born into the Danish royal family, Martha was the daughter of King Eric V of Denmark and sister of King Eric VI. She was given the name Margrete at birth, but in Sweden was called Märta. Martha was a politically influential queen, playing a key role in the Håtuna games and the Nyköping Banquet. Her marriage to King Birger cemented her status as a member of the Swedish royal family.

Martha's influence extended beyond her marriage, as she participated in the Håtuna games, a medieval festival that showcased the region's strength and martial prowess. She was also a prominent figure in the Nyköping Banquet, a lavish feast that celebrated the union between Sweden and Denmark. These events demonstrate Martha's position as a respected leader in medieval Sweden.

Martha's legacy is complex, as she was both a powerful queen and a member of the Danish royal family. Her marriage to King Birger influenced the succession of the Swedish throne, as her brother Eric VI succeeded Birger after his death. Martha's role in the Håtuna games and the Nyköping Banquet also left a lasting impact on Swedish culture and tradition.

Martha of Denmark's impact on Swedish history is evident in her enduring legacy as a queen and a symbol of the region's rich cultural heritage. Her story serves as a reminder of the intricate web of alliances and power struggles that defined medieval Europe.

Martha of Denmark's life was marked by significant events, including her marriage to King Birger and her participation in the Håtuna games and the Nyköping Banquet. These events demonstrate her influence and position within the Swedish royal family.
